system:
You are the test planner of a network change-validation pipeline. Given the change ticket, the
intent analysis and the configuration diff, write a change-specific test plan that (a) checks every effect the ticket
promises and (b) checks that nothing else that the diff could affect has changed (use expect "unchanged").
Also consider emulation-only risks: MTU (mtu probes), failover timers (conv), link load after path changes (load).
Typed test language (JSON objects; use ONLY these types and only names that exist):
  {"t":"reach","src":HOST,"dst":HOST|ROUTER,"svc":SVC|"*","expect":"allow"|"deny"|"unchanged"}
  {"t":"path","src":HOST,"dst":HOST,"via":ROUTER,"expect":true|false}
  {"t":"route","dev":ROUTER,"prefix":"a.b.c.d/n","expect":"present"|"absent"|"unchanged"}
  {"t":"adj","a":ROUTER,"b":ROUTER,"expect":"up"|"down"|"unchanged"}          (OSPF adjacency on a link)
  {"t":"mtu","src":HOST,"dst":HOST,"size":1500|9000,"expect":"pass"|"fail"}  (DF probe, emulation tier)
  {"t":"conv","a":ROUTER,"b":ROUTER,"max_s":3}                               (failover time of a link, emulation)
  {"t":"load","a":ROUTER,"b":ROUTER,"max_pct":90}                            (link utilisation, emulation)
  {"t":"like","host":HOST,"as":HOST}     (after a VLAN move / re-addressing: host has exactly the same access as the
                                          reference host, towards and from every other host and service)
SVC is one of: icmp, tcp/22, tcp/25, tcp/80, tcp/443, tcp/5432, udp/53.
Reply with JSON only: {"tests": [ ... ]}

CHANGE TICKET:
Shift the c1-host to c2-host traffic away from the SEA-CHM link.

INTENT ANALYSIS:
{"ticket_says": "Move traffic between c1-host and c2-host off the SEA-CHM link, so it takes a different path.", "goal": "Reroute c1-host to c2-host traffic so it no longer traverses the SEA-CHM link.", "change_type": "ospf", "scope": ["c1-host", "c2-host", "SEA", "CHM"], "expected_effects": ["Traffic from c1-host to c2-host no longer traverses the SEA-CHM link", "c1-host to c2-host connectivity still works via an alternate path"], "must_not_change": [], "confidence": "medium"}

CONFIG DIFF:
CHM | interface eth1 | - ip ospf cost 10
CHM | interface eth1 | + ip ospf cost 1
SEA | interface eth3 | - ip ospf cost 10
SEA | interface eth3 | + ip ospf cost 1

TOPOLOGY (2-hop around changed devices): devices ['ATL', 'BOU', 'CHM', 'CPK', 'HOU', 'ITH', 'LNK', 'PAO', 'PIT', 'SDG', 'SEA', 'SLC', 'cust1', 'peer1', 'peer2']; hosts ['c1-host']; links ['SEA--PAO (10000 Mbps)', 'SEA--SDG (10000 Mbps)', 'SEA--CHM (10000 Mbps)', 'PAO--SDG (10000 Mbps)', 'PAO--SLC (10000 Mbps)', 'SDG--HOU (10000 Mbps)', 'SLC--BOU (10000 Mbps)', 'BOU--HOU (2500 Mbps)', 'BOU--LNK (10000 Mbps)', 'HOU--ATL (10000 Mbps)', 'LNK--CHM (2500 Mbps)', 'CHM--PIT (10000 Mbps)', 'PIT--ATL (10000 Mbps)', 'PIT--ITH (10000 Mbps)', 'PIT--CPK (10000 Mbps)', 'SEA--cust1 (10000 Mbps)', 'PIT--peer1 (10000 Mbps)', 'PAO--peer2 (10000 Mbps)']
Hosts: c1-host(172.16.1.10,cust1,mtu 1500), c2-host(172.16.2.10,cust2,mtu 1500), c3-host(172.16.3.10,cust3,mtu 1500), ext-dns1(8.8.8.10,internet,mtu 1500), ext-dns2(1.1.1.10,internet,mtu 1500), noc1(10.99.0.10,noc,mtu 1500), noc2(10.99.0.11,noc,mtu 1500), noclab1(10.98.0.10,noc-lab,mtu 1500), noclab2(10.98.0.11,noc-lab,mtu 1500)
Routers: SEA, PAO, SDG, SLC, BOU, HOU, LNK, CHM, PIT, ATL, AAR, ITH, PRN, CPK, cust1, cust2, cust3, peer1, peer2
Network invariants (always checked): no forwarding loops; management host noc1 reaches every managed router; isolation pairs must stay blocked: [['c1-host', 'noc1'], ['ext-dns1', 'noc1'], ['c3-host', 'noc1'], ['ext-dns2', 'noclab1']]; external peers ['peer1', 'peer2', 'cust1', 'cust2', 'cust3'] must not learn ['10.0.0.0/8']; SLAs: failover <= 3.0 s, link utilisation <= 90.0%.
text:
The diff lowers the OSPF cost from 10 to 1 on the SEA-CHM link (CHM eth1, SEA eth3), which makes that link MORE attractive. The ticket asks to move c1-host to c2-host traffic OFF the SEA-CHM link. The diff appears to do the opposite, so the plan checks the ticket's promised effects (the path avoids the SEA-CHM link, connectivity remains) and also checks for collateral changes.

Topology notes: c1-host sits behind cust1, attached to SEA. c2-host sits behind cust2, whose attachment point is not shown. CHM is likely near cust2, since the 2-hop view lists PIT and peer1 on that side. The alternate paths around CHM are SEA-PAO/SDG and then SLC, BOU, LNK, and into CHM via the LNK link, or via HOU, ATL and PIT. Because I cannot be sure which routers the path traverses, I use the SEA and CHM endpoints in the path tests.

```json
{"tests": [
  {"t":"adj","a":"SEA","b":"CHM","expect":"up"},
  {"t":"path","src":"c1-host","dst":"c2-host","via":"CHM","expect":false},
  {"t":"path","src":"c2-host","dst":"c1-host","via":"CHM","expect":false},
  {"t":"reach","src":"c1-host","dst":"c2-host","svc":"icmp","expect":"allow"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"c2-host","dst":"c1-host","svc":"icmp","expect":"allow"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"c1-host","dst":"c2-host","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"c2-host","dst":"c1-host","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"c1-host","dst":"c3-host","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"c3-host","dst":"c1-host","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"c2-host","dst":"c3-host","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"c1-host","dst":"ext-dns1","svc":"udp/53","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"c1-host","dst":"noc1","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"noc1","dst":"CHM","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"reach","src":"noc1","dst":"SEA","svc":"*","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"SEA","prefix":"172.16.2.0/24","expect":"present"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"CHM","prefix":"172.16.1.0/24","expect":"present"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"PIT","prefix":"172.16.1.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"route","dev":"PAO","prefix":"172.16.2.0/24","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"adj","a":"SEA","b":"PAO","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"adj","a":"SEA","b":"SDG","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"adj","a":"CHM","b":"LNK","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"adj","a":"CHM","b":"PIT","expect":"unchanged"},
  {"t":"mtu","src":"c1-host","dst":"c2-host","size":1500,"expect":"pass"},
  {"t":"conv","a":"SEA","b":"CHM","max_s":3},
  {"t":"conv","a":"SEA","b":"PAO","max_s":3},
  {"t":"load","a":"SEA","b":"CHM","max_pct":90},
  {"t":"load","a":"SEA","b":"PAO","max_pct":90},
  {"t":"load","a":"SEA","b":"SDG","max_pct":90},
  {"t":"load","a":"LNK","b":"CHM","max_pct":90}
]}
```

The first two path tests are the key ones. If the diff is applied as written, they should fail, because lowering the cost to 1 pulls traffic onto SEA-CHM rather than away from it. That would show the change contradicts the ticket (it should likely have raised the cost).
